concept.title: People with disabilities or additional needs
concept.shortdesc: Children and adults with learning, physical, sensory or neurodevelopmental disabilities and special educational needs, and their families.

conbody.note: Draft group. Groups are a convenience for browsing the draft: the hierarchy was proposed by a second clustering pass and named by a language model, and no person has reviewed it.

ul.li: : Neurodivergent children, young people and adults, including those with autism, ADHD and related conditions, and the parents or carers who support them.
: Autistic people of any age, including those on the autistic spectrum or with Asperger Syndrome, and their families.
: Families or parents of a child or young person, up to age 25, who has special educational needs or disabilities.
: People with a learning disability or learning difficulty, of any age but mostly adults.
: Adults with a learning disability and/or autism, sometimes with other conditions such as physical disability or complex needs, often for care and housing.
: People with a disability or a physical or mental health condition, often listed together with other barriers such as neurodiversity or barriers to work.
: Adults (sometimes teenagers) who have both a learning disability and a physical disability, including those with severe needs who require accommodation and personal care.
: People who are blind, partially sighted or have other vision loss, along with people with sight and/or hearing loss or sensory impairments generally.
: Children and young people with a disability, special needs or a named condition such as Down's syndrome or cerebral palsy, and sometimes their families.
: Children and young people, often up to age 25, described in full as having special educational needs and disabilities, including those who receive support in school or early years.
: Children, young people up to 25 and their families described using the abbreviation SEND (or SEN).
